source_title: Trump says 'millions of barrels' of oil transited through Hormuz

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said an IRGC general's claim that the Strait of Hormuz was closed and under Iranian control was false, that traffic was flowing, and that the United States and regional partners clearly controlled the strait.
notes: Quote: 'CLAIM: ... "the Strait of Hormuz is closed" ... This is FALSE. FACT: Traffic is flowing through the Strait of Hormuz right now carrying commercial goods and energy supplies... The United States and regional partners clearly control the strait.' Posted the day Iran's IRGC asserted closure; Iran disputes.
source_title: US CENTCOM rejects Iran's claim of Hormuz closure, says 20 million barrels of crude moving through

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said traffic flowing through the strait included 20 million barrels of crude oil.
notes: Quote: '...including 20 million barrels of crude oil.' Time basis not stated ('right now'); unclear whether a day, a night or vessels in transit.
source_title: US CENTCOM rejects Iran's claim of Hormuz closure, says 20 million barrels of crude moving through

speaker: Marco Rubio
claim_text: Said the Strait of Hormuz was open and that Iran had lost complete control of it.
notes: Quote: 'The Strait of Hormuz is open... So they've lost complete control of the strait.' CBS live updates timed the remarks at 7:18 AM ET.
source_title: Iran has 'lost complete control' of Strait of Hormuz, US claims

speaker: Marco Rubio
claim_text: Said there was almost as much oil flowing out of the strait now as there was before the conflict began.
notes: Quote: 'There's almost as much oil flowing out now as there was before this conflict began.' No figure. Kpler's seven-day Middle East crude export average was 18.3 million barrels per day on Sep 30 vs about 18 million pre-war (per The National).
source_title: Iran has 'lost complete control' of Strait of Hormuz, US claims

speaker: Donald Trump
claim_text: Said oil was flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait, 22 million barrels the previous night alone.
notes: Post of 12:45 PM EDT (per CBS News live updates). Quote: '...with oil flowing in record numbers of barrels through the Hormuz Strait (22 million barrels, last night alone, with not one barrel coming from, or going to, Iran), we will not be attacking Iran at any time prior to the midterm elections...' Previous night was Oct 7. Exceeds the roughly 20 million barrels a day the strait carried before the war. Shipping Telegraph and Axios also reported the post.
source_title: Donald Trump says US will not launch strikes against Iran before midterms

speaker: Donald Trump
claim_text: Said not one barrel of the previous night's oil was coming from, or going to, Iran, and that the blockade would remain in full force.
notes: Same post as USOF-20261008-01.
source_title: Donald Trump says US will not launch strikes against Iran before midterms

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said U.S. forces had secured the transport of more than 1.25 billion barrels of crude oil from Gulf partners through the Strait of Hormuz in recent months.
notes: Value recorded as 1250 million barrels. Quote (translated): 'In recent months, US forces have secured the transportation of more than 1.25 billion barrels of crude oil from partners in the Persian Gulf region through the Strait of Hormuz.' Also said thousands of commercial vessels had passed safely. Later reading of the same cumulative series as USOF-20260919-01. Also reported by IranWire.
source_title: CENTCOM announced assistance in transporting 1.25 billion barrels of oil through Hormuz

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said Iranian oil exports from its ports had ground to a halt under the U.S. blockade.
notes: Qualitative; no figure in the report.
source_title: CENTCOM announced assistance in transporting 1.25 billion barrels of oil through Hormuz

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said U.S. forces had redirected 133 commercial vessels as of October 9 to ensure compliance with the blockade.
notes: Quote: 'As of Oct. 9, U.S. forces have redirected 133 commercial vessels to ensure compliance.'
source_title: CENTCOM: US redirects 133 vessels under Iran blockade

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said a U.S. fighter jet had disabled the Panama-flagged cargo vessel Ocean Molica in the Gulf of Oman after it left an Iranian port and tried to run the blockade.
notes: Also known as 'Arika Sun'. Struck on the stern to disable propulsion; CENTCOM said no crew were harmed. CENTCOM X post: https://x.com/CENTCOM/status/2109073217176637447. Also reported by The Hill.
source_title: US military says it disabled vessel attempting to violate blockade

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said four commercial vessels had now been disabled during three months of blockade enforcement.
source_title: US military says it disabled vessel attempting to violate blockade

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said 135 ships had been turned around during three months of strict blockade enforcement.
notes: Wikipedia cites the same figure from CENTCOM for Oct 10.
source_title: US military says it disabled vessel attempting to violate blockade

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said 10 tankers linked to IRGC operations had been destroyed.
notes: Differs from the Oct 5 count of 13 commercial vessels destroyed over 12 weeks (USOF-20261005-03); categories may differ (tankers vs all vessels). Recorded side by side, not as a correction.
source_title: US military says it disabled vessel attempting to violate blockade

speaker: Chris Wright
claim_text: Said oil flows through the Strait of Hormuz had returned to 80 to 90 percent of pre-conflict levels.
notes: Remarks at the 25th WPC Energy Congress in Riyadh on 12 October. Asharq Al-Awsat gives 80 to 90 percent for oil against 25 to 35 percent for refined products. Kpler's September average for Hormuz oil exports, cited in the same reporting, was just under 9 million barrels a day, about 44 percent of pre-war.
source_title: US Energy Secretary: Oil Flows Through Hormuz Reach 80-90% of Pre-Conflict Levels

speaker: Chris Wright
claim_text: Said up to 14 million barrels of oil a day were moving through the Strait of Hormuz.
notes: The National reports the figure as up to 14 million barrels a day; another account of the same remarks renders it as 13 to 14 million. Recorded as 14 because the report states it as the level reached. Kpler's seven-day average to 13 October was 11.62 million barrels a day (estimate e23). Enters the comparable series; site ledger row c11.
source_title: US says Hormuz oil flows recover to 14 million bpd despite Saudi attacks

speaker: Chris Wright
claim_text: Said flows of refined petroleum products out of the Gulf were 25 to 35 percent of their pre-conflict level.
notes: Said in the same remarks as USOF-20261012-01. Wright called products the bigger problem.
source_title: US Energy Secretary: Oil Flows Through Hormuz Reach 80-90% of Pre-Conflict Levels

speaker: Chris Wright
claim_text: Said additional Gulf supplies were also moving through pipelines that bypass the Strait of Hormuz.
notes: No figure given. Saudi Arabia told the same conference it planned to raise East-West pipeline capacity to 10 million barrels a day within two to three years; that is a Saudi statement, not a U.S. one, and is not recorded here.
source_title: US says Hormuz oil flows recover to 14 million bpd despite Saudi attacks

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said the United States and regional partners clearly controlled the Strait of Hormuz.
notes: Posted on Tuesday 13 October, answering IRGC Navy commander Rear Adm. Ali Ozmaei, who said the strait was under IRGC control and that any U.S. warship approaching would be sunk. Iran disputes.
source_title: CENTCOM says US helped ship 19 million barrels through Hormuz Monday

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said U.S. forces had helped Gulf partners ship more than 19 million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz on Monday.
notes: Monday was 12 October. Iran International and Arab Times render it 'more than 19 million barrels'; Gulf News renders it as 19 million barrels transiting on Monday, so no upper value is recorded. Six days earlier CENTCOM gave 20 million barrels with no stated basis (USOF-20261007-02).
source_title: CENTCOM says US helped ship 19 million barrels through Hormuz Monday

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said the United States and regional partners controlled the strait and that commercial vessels continued to transit despite IRGC attacks.
notes: One of three Iranian claims the post called false: that the IRGC controls the strait, that a mine sank the GFS Pride, and a claim about U.S. military deaths. The post's X id 2110780675238289548 times it at 17:11 UTC on 15 October.
source_title: CENTCOM rejects Iran's claims on Hormuz, cargo ship sinking and US deaths

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said more than 40 commercial ships had moved through the Strait of Hormuz in the past 24 hours.
notes: The Joint Maritime Information Center counted 121 U.S.-facilitated transits over the four days 11 to 14 October, about 30 a day, against a 2025 benchmark of about 138 a day.
source_title: CENTCOM rejects Iran's claims on Hormuz, cargo ship sinking and US deaths

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said an IRGC projectile, not a naval mine, had struck the Singapore-flagged container ship GFS Pride, which sank while being towed to shore.
notes: The IRGC said the ship struck a mine. All 21 crew were evacuated without injury. Accounts put the strike on 13 or 14 October and the sinking on 14 or 15 October; this ledger does not pick between them. The Iranian account is not a row here, so no disputes link is recorded.
source_title: CENTCOM rejects Iran's claims on Hormuz, cargo ship sinking and US deaths

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said the strait's primary transit routes remained clear of mines.
notes: CENTCOM's wording is about the primary routes; some accounts render it as the strait having been cleared of mines. Iran said on 18 October that two tankers caught fire after striking mines.
source_title: CENTCOM rejects Iran's claims on Hormuz, cargo ship sinking and US deaths

speaker: Adm. Brad Cooper
claim_text: Said about 400 merchant ships had transited the Strait of Hormuz over the past seven days.
notes: Cooper did not say which seven days. UKMTO counted 254 transits for the seven days to 14 October, 42 of them tracked by AIS and 212 of them U.S.-reported facilitated transits that UKMTO said it "cannot independently verify".
source_title: 'Vast majority' of Iran's attempted attacks on Strait of Hormuz are unsuccessful, CENTCOM spokesman says

speaker: Adm. Brad Cooper
claim_text: Said U.S. forces had helped Gulf partners move more than 100 million barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz over the past seven days.
notes: Said in the same video as USOF-20261016-01. Kpler's seven-day average to 13 October was 11.62 million barrels a day (estimate e23); the two figures are on different bases and this ledger does not convert between them.
source_title: “Let Me Be Clear”: CENTCOM Chief’s Rosy Hormuz Video Collides With Reality

speaker: Adm. Brad Cooper
claim_text: Said U.S. forces had helped move more than 1.3 billion barrels of crude oil through the Strait of Hormuz in recent months.
notes: Value recorded as 1300 million barrels. Later reading of the same cumulative series as USOF-20260919-01 (1 billion) and USOF-20261008-03 (1.25 billion). One account dates the total from the start of the war rather than from recent months.
source_title: “Let Me Be Clear”: CENTCOM Chief’s Rosy Hormuz Video Collides With Reality

speaker: Adm. Brad Cooper
claim_text: Said U.S. forces had kept Iran from exporting at least 25 billion dollars worth of crude oil.
notes: Cooper gave no valuation method and no start date. In the same video he said nearly 350 million dollars in cryptocurrency assets had been frozen with CENTCOM support; that figure is not about oil or shipping and is not recorded here.
source_title: Centcom commander says naval blockade cost Iran $25B in oil revenue

speaker: Adm. Brad Cooper
claim_text: Said that apart from humanitarian assistance allowed in, Iran had no exports and no imports by sea.
notes: Quote: 'with the exception of the humanitarian assistance we've allowed in, Iran has no exports and no imports by sea.'
source_title: Centcom commander says naval blockade cost Iran $25B in oil revenue

speaker: Adm. Brad Cooper
claim_text: Said Iranian attacks on commercial shipping had killed more than 20 civilian mariners since the war began on 28 February.
notes: Cooper cited the International Maritime Organization's count, so the figure is the IMO's and not a U.S. tally. Kept because it is a numbered claim about shipping through the strait.
source_title: 'Vast majority' of Iran's attempted attacks on Strait of Hormuz are unsuccessful, CENTCOM spokesman says

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said U.S. forces had redirected 138 commercial vessels as of October 17 to ensure strict compliance with the blockade.
notes: Quote: 'As of Oct. 17, CENTCOM forces have redirected 138 commercial vessels to ensure strict compliance.' Kurdistan24 dates the count from the resumption of the blockade on 14 July.
source_title: CENTCOM Reports 138 Vessels Redirected to Enforce Iran Blockade

speaker: Capt. Tim Hawkins
claim_text: Said the Strait of Hormuz was open and available for transit and that transits had continued that day.
notes: Quote: 'It is open, it is available for transit, and we've seen that transit continue this very day.' Said after the GFS Pride sank. One outlet dated the remarks 18 October.
source_title: 'Vast majority' of Iran's attempted attacks on Strait of Hormuz are unsuccessful, CENTCOM spokesman says

speaker: Capt. Tim Hawkins
claim_text: Said about 97 percent of the ships that had sought to transit the Strait of Hormuz had done so without being hit by an Iranian projectile.
notes: The share counts only whether a ship was struck by a projectile, not traffic against normal. UKMTO logged 12 attacks in its latest period, 10 of them in the strait, and said most attacks go unreported. Iran International counted at least 10 ships struck since 11 October.
source_title: 'Vast majority' of Iran's attempted attacks on Strait of Hormuz are unsuccessful, CENTCOM spokesman says

speaker: JD Vance
claim_text: Said the U.S. Navy was keeping oil and gas moving out of the Strait of Hormuz and that gasoline prices would be three times as high without it.
notes: Quote: 'They would be three times as high if it weren't for the United States Navy keeping oil and gas moving out of the Strait of Hormuz.' No flow figure. Vance also said prices would fall once the war was over and that gas prices were too high.
source_title: JD Vance says petrol prices would be 'three times as high' without US Navy

speaker: Chris Wright
claim_text: Said the seven-day average of oil and oil products leaving the strait by ship was just under 11 million barrels a day as of that morning, the highest since the start of the conflict.
notes: Quote: 'just under 11 million barrels a day, seven-day average of oil and oil products going out of the Strait on ship on water.' Reported by TASS, published 22:57 UTC on 9 September with a 10 September dateline. A later reading of the seven-day series after USOF-20260821-02 and before USOF-20260913-01 (10); not a correction.
source_title: Nearly 11 mln barrels of oil transit Strait of Hormuz daily — US energy secretary

speaker: Chris Wright
claim_text: Said another three to five million barrels a day were moving through the bypass pipelines.
notes: Bypass component; not Hormuz flow. Below the 4-5 given 1 September (USOF-20260901-02); different dates, not recorded as a correction.
source_title: Nearly 11 mln barrels of oil transit Strait of Hormuz daily — US energy secretary

speaker: Marco Rubio
claim_text: Said roughly 13 to 14 million barrels a day had moved through the Strait of Hormuz over the last ten days, and more so over the last thirty.
notes: Rubio gave the interview on 15 October; the State Department published the transcript on 19 October, which is why it enters the ledger after the statements of 16 and 17 October. Breitbart's own write-up is dated 18 October and places the sit-down late the previous week. Rubio gave one window of ten days and a second of thirty; the row carries the ten-day window he named first. Kpler's Hormuz reading for the week to 14 October was 9.4 million barrels a day (estimate e34) and its reading for the week to 18 October about 14 (e35). Wright gave 13 to 14 million barrels a day on 12 October (USOF-20261012-02); a different speaker on a different window, so no link is recorded.
source_title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio With Matthew Boyle of Breitbart News

speaker: Marco Rubio
claim_text: Said the flow through the strait had reached pre-conflict levels on some days.
notes: Rubio gave the interview on 15 October; the State Department published the transcript on 19 October, which is why it enters the ledger after the statements of 16 and 17 October. Breitbart's own write-up is dated 18 October and places the sit-down late the previous week. No figure for the pre-conflict level and no dates for the days he meant. Said in the same interview as USOF-20261015-05.
source_title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio With Matthew Boyle of Breitbart News

speaker: Marco Rubio
claim_text: Said Iranian oil was blocked from moving through the Strait of Hormuz while other countries' oil kept flowing.
notes: Rubio gave the interview on 15 October; the State Department published the transcript on 19 October, which is why it enters the ledger after the statements of 16 and 17 October. Breitbart's own write-up is dated 18 October and places the sit-down late the previous week. No figure for the Iranian volume blocked. IANS, which carried the transcript on 20 October, noted that the statement came without shipping data behind it.
source_title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio With Matthew Boyle of Breitbart News

speaker: Marco Rubio
claim_text: Said U.S. forces were escorting and protecting commercial ships against Iranian attacks.
notes: Rubio gave the interview on 15 October; the State Department published the transcript on 19 October, which is why it enters the ledger after the statements of 16 and 17 October. Breitbart's own write-up is dated 18 October and places the sit-down late the previous week. No count of escorted ships. CENTCOM said on 26 May that Project Freedom had not resumed and that U.S. forces were not then escorting commercial vessels; that statement is not in this ledger and the two are months apart.
source_title: Secretary of State Marco Rubio With Matthew Boyle of Breitbart News

speaker: Donald Trump
claim_text: Said more oil was coming through the Hormuz Strait now than before the conflict began.
notes: Quote: 'they are even making up fake hits, mines, and everything else, because more Oil is coming through the Hormuz Strait now than it did even prior to the beginning of the Conflict.' No figure. Posted the day the IRGC said it had attacked four vessels and that three more had struck mines; Brent rose about 4 percent to 113 dollars.
source_title: Trump accuses Iran of making up fake strikes on ships to drive up oil prices

speaker: Donald Trump
claim_text: Said Iran was making up fake hits and mines in the Strait of Hormuz to drive up the price of oil before the midterm elections.
notes: Quote: 'they are even making up fake hits, mines, and everything else, because more Oil is coming through the Hormuz Strait now than it did even prior to the beginning of the Conflict.' Said in the same post as USOF-20261022-01. The UK Maritime Trade Operations logged more than two dozen attacks on ships in October, a record, and said most attacked vessels do not report. The Iranian account is not a row here, so no disputes link is recorded.
source_title: Trump accuses Iran of making up fake strikes on ships to drive up oil prices

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said the blockade had helped prevent Iran from exporting at least 25 billion dollars worth of crude oil.
notes: Posted to mark 100 days since the blockade resumed. The same figure Adm. Brad Cooper gave on 16 October (USOF-20261016-04); the value is unchanged, so this is a restatement by the institution and not a revision, and no supersedes link is recorded. No valuation method and no start date given in either statement.
source_title: Trump accuses Iran of making up fake strikes on ships to drive up oil prices

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said 100 days had passed since CENTCOM forces resumed the naval blockade of Iran.
notes: Quote: 'Today marks 100 days since CENTCOM forces resumed America's steel wall naval blockade against Iran.' Counting back 100 days from 22 October gives 14 July, the date Kurdistan24 gave for the resumption when CENTCOM published its vessel-redirection count (USOF-20261017-01). One account dates the resumption to 15 July.
source_title: Trump accuses Iran of making up fake strikes on ships to drive up oil prices

speaker: U.S. Central Command
claim_text: Said there had been no exports or imports to Iran by sea except the humanitarian aid U.S. forces had allowed in.
notes: Said in the same post as USOF-20261022-03 and USOF-20261022-04. The same claim Adm. Brad Cooper made on 16 October (USOF-20261016-05).
source_title: Trump accuses Iran of making up fake strikes on ships to drive up oil prices

speaker: Donald Trump
claim_text: Said the Strait of Hormuz was totally the United States' and that the United States would keep it that way.
notes: Quote as carried by Fox News: 'And that's the way we'll keep it.' Said in the same remarks as USOF-20261023-02, in which he also said the United States could take Iran's oil and the whole country. The IRGC said the same week that it controlled the strait. At a rally in Fort Myers, Florida, later the same day he again put the strait under full U.S. control; that is the same claim and is not a separate row.
source_title: Trump said U.S. could 'just take' all Iran's oil as Tehran threatens escalation if attacked

speaker: Donald Trump
claim_text: Said more oil was moving through the Strait of Hormuz than before the war.
notes: No figure. The same claim he posted the day before (USOF-20261022-01); neither carries a number, so neither revises the other and no link is recorded. Kpler's reading for the week to 18 October put Hormuz at about 82 percent of the pre-war level (estimate e35) and the region including bypass routes above it (e36).
source_title: Trump said U.S. could 'just take' all Iran's oil as Tehran threatens escalation if attacked

speaker: Scott Bessent
claim_text: Said oil exports from the Persian Gulf had surpassed pre-conflict levels.
notes: Quote: 'Despite Iran's efforts to disrupt energy shipments, oil exports from the Persian Gulf are roaring back and have surpassed pre-conflict levels. The message is clear: Iran's threats have failed to stop the flow of energy to global markets.' Persian Gulf exports, not Hormuz alone, so it is not comparable with the strait figures. ANI reported the post from Washington on 24 October.
source_title: Despite Iran's efforts to disrupt energy shipments, oil exports from the Persian Gulf are roaring back

speaker: Scott Bessent
claim_text: Said a Treasury chart posted with the statement showed crude and condensate exports through Hormuz, the Gulf of Oman and the Red Sea of about 17 to 18 million barrels a day.
notes: Figure read from the chart posted with USOF-20261023-03, as Fox News reported it; the text of the post carries no number. Accounts differ on the period: Fox News reads the chart as the current level, SANA puts 17 to 18 million barrels a day at the end of September. Regional scope including the Red Sea, so it is not a Hormuz-only figure. Kpler put the same kind of regional flow at 24.6 million barrels a day for the week to 18 October (estimate e36) and Vortexa at 18 (e37); the three count different water and this ledger does not convert between them.
source_title: Netanyahu calls for US and Israel to overthrow Iran as Brent crude hits five-month high
